findings.location: Design section 1, lines 96-105; Requirement-to-Design/Test Matrix, lines 263-267
findings.affected_requirement: Prior PLR-001; Story 4.3 AC-1/AC-3/AC-6; spec FR-001, FR-007, FR-011, FR-013; canonical Profiled Revision invariant
findings.evidence: The correction captures HEAD and verifies that the revision name does not change, but that does not prove the Repository profile was derived from that commit. The current CodeGraphContextProvider indexes the mutable workingCopyPath and reads local file bytes, while GitWorkingCopyService reuses a checkout that may contain uncommitted changes. An uncommitted mutation leaves HEAD unchanged, so every proposed revision check can pass while CodeGraph profile facts come from bytes different from the Profiled Revision and the detector reads committed Git blobs. The advancement test covers a moved HEAD but not this unchanged-HEAD mismatch.
findings.correction_outcome: Make the complete profile and detector consume one immutable committed tree, or fail closed by proving and maintaining a clean locked checkout for the whole profile transaction. Add a test that mutates tracked working-copy bytes without moving HEAD and proves no approved result is published, alongside the existing commit-advancement and downstream-consumer mismatch tests.

findings.location: Summary lines 16-19 and Migration and parallel-story ordering lines 181-196
findings.affected_requirement: Story 4.3 migration ownership; Story 11.1 migration dependency; expedited-MVP three-checkpoint authority; July 30 delivery sequence
findings.evidence: The plan releases Story 4.3 ownership of VulgataDbContext, the model snapshot, and migrations at the accepted-delivery-definition checkpoint and directs Story 11.1 to branch or rebase from that SHA. Under the expedited authority, that first checkpoint contains story/spec/plan/authorization/tasks and occurs before implementation. Story 4.3's AddConservativePreScanGate migration therefore does not exist at the SHA from which Story 11.1 is told to begin migration work. Both stories can subsequently edit the same DbContext and snapshot, recreating the migration-order divergence the serialization rule is intended to prevent. The approved July 30 sequence places Story 4.3 before Story 11.1.
findings.correction_outcome: Keep Story 11.1 migration, DbContext, and model-snapshot work blocked until Story 4.3's migration is implemented and durable on the completed-story checkpoint, then require Story 11.1 to branch or rebase from that exact SHA. Story 11.1 may continue non-overlapping specification and planning work meanwhile.

findings.affected_requirement: Story 4.3 AC-2/AC-4; spec User Story 2 scenario 2, FR-007, FR-010, FR-013, SC-005
findings.evidence: The corrected detector reserves and persists direct Confirmed samples, but the Pre-Scan Handoff schema exposes only confirmedKinds flags plus hint and warning arrays. It has no bounded Confirmed classification or confirmed-evidence collection, so an authorized consumer cannot receive the Evidence Locator, confidence, rule, and provenance for confirmed kinds required by the specification's typed approved-result scenario. The flags correctly preserve truth after truncation, but they do not satisfy the required auditable confirmed evidence contract.
findings.correction_outcome: Add a bounded, ordered confirmed-evidence projection to the Core read model, Shared DTO, handoff contract, mapping, redaction rules, and tests. Keep confirmedKinds derived solely from the persisted flags, and verify the more-than-100 both-kind case returns both flags plus one deterministic reserved direct sample for each confirmed kind.

summary: REVISE. The corrected set resolves the prior circular detector/composite defect, Core-to-Web-to-Shared dependency seam, confirmed-kind truth truncation mechanism, and canonical glossary gap. It also correctly excludes new routes, agent tools, dispatch, LLM/HITL behavior, endpoint resolution, and Communication Pattern Catalog management, and it retains planned-change authorization, TDD, security, migration checks, combined review, and current-boundary integration verification. Advancement remains unsafe because the Profiled Revision checks do not bind the mutable CodeGraph profile to committed bytes, Story 4.3 releases shared migration ownership before its migration is implemented, and the typed handoff omits confirmed evidence required by the accepted specification.
